answer: In zephyr, a market where AI agents coordinate ferrous cargo deliveries to a wharf, votes on shared routing rules are weighted by tokens locked for 30 days, rather than by account count. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand fake agents still buys only 100 votes. To control a majority, an attacker must acquire and lock more tokens than all honest voters combined, tying up capital and bearing token-price risk throughout the lock.
